item.title: Council materials: women's underground work restrictions and draft equal employment policy
item.description: AI summary: The Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare announced publication of materials for the 94th Labour Policy Council Subcommittee on Employment Environment and Equal Employment on 2026-11-26; the excerpts are dated 2026-11-27. An interim research report describes existing restrictions: pregnant and postpartum women are prohibited from all underground work, while other women aged 18 or over are restricted from excavation, blasting and associated work but may perform management and supervisory duties. Citing mechanization and improved safety management, the report supports considering a review of restrictions for women other than pregnant and postpartum women, conditional on adequate safety standards, retained protective rules, information, training and suitable equipment; it does not establish a regulatory change. Separate materials summarize 55 public comments on the draft Basic Policy on Equal Employment Opportunity Measures for Men and Women, submitted during 2026-10-09 to 2026-11-07, including views on pay-gap analysis, career opportunities, work-family support and harassment prevention. item.title: Draft ordinance, notice and circular amendments on automated vehicles and vehicle safety standards
item.description: AI summary: On 2026-11-19, the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism published draft Ministerial Ordinance, Notice and circular amendments concerning vehicle safety standards and procedures for assigning operational-environment conditions; the stated comment deadline is 2026-12-19 10:00 JST, and the contact is the Vehicle Standards and International Affairs Division, Logistics and Motor Vehicles Bureau. The proposed amendments to the Safety Regulations for Road Vehicles (Ministry of Transport Ordinance No. 67 of 1951), under the Road Transport Vehicle Act (Act No. 185 of 1951), would define two categories of automated-operation vehicles that cannot exceed 6 km/h without using their automated driving systems: Type 1 with passenger capacity and Type 2 without passenger capacity; they would also revise provisions assuming a driver's seat and exclude Type 2 vehicles from specified occupant-protection standards. The draft Notice would apply UN Regulation No. 185 requirements to vehicles equipped with automated driving systems, excluding large and small special motor vehicles, and establish color, brightness and other standards for devices projecting turning or lane-change intentions onto the road. Related ordinance amendments would permit documentary conformity checks for underrun-protection devices and direction-indication projection devices during initial inspections, expand equipment type-designation provisions, and add safety-management capability criteria and certification forms for permission for specified modifications involving automated driving systems. The ordinance outline schedules promulgation for 2026-12-25 and commencement for 2026-12-27, with automated-driving-system provisions concerning equipment type designation, fees and specified-modification permissions scheduled for 2027-01-30; these are proposed dates, not confirmation of promulgation or commencement. Original title: 道路運送車両の保安基準等の一部を改正する省令案、道路運送車両の保安基準の細目を定める告示等の一部を改正する告示案及び走行環境条件の付与の実施要領について（依命通達）の一部を改正する案について Public Comment Open | e-Gov Public Comment | Published 2026-11-19 | First detected 2026-11-20 Monitoring aid only; not legal advice or an official translation. item.title: Environment Minister's opinion on draft assessment for Isa–Ebino–Hitoyoshi wind project
item.description: AI summary: On 2026-11-12, the Ministry of the Environment announced submission of the Environment Minister's opinion on the draft environmental impact assessment for the tentatively named Isa–Ebino–Hitoyoshi Wind Power Project. Green Power Investment Corporation proposes up to 28 turbines totaling 117,600 kW across Isa, Kagoshima Prefecture; Ebino, Miyazaki Prefecture; and Hitoyoshi, Kumamoto Prefecture.
